outcomeTiers.explanation: You never let urgency or trust override your judgment — and you were decisive about it. That's the difference between being suspicious and being savvy.
You caught the trap in the end, even if it took a moment to get there. Good instincts, slightly slow trigger.
You got out — but only after giving the con more room than it needed.
You spotted the oldest trick in the book, too late. The promise was huge. The first ask was small. That's the point.

start.message: Good afternoon. My name is Adewale Okoro and I am acting on behalf of the estate of Mr. Samuel Williams. Your email address was identified during our beneficiary verification process. You are entitled to a payment of £4,200,000. Please confirm that this email address belongs to you so that I can explain the next steps.

choices.label: Yes, that's my email. Tell me more.
How did you get my details?
I wasn't expecting anything like this. I'll need to verify this independently.
This sounds like a scam.

engage.message: Thank you for confirming. To proceed, I will need your full name, address and telephone number.

choices.label: Sure, here's my information.
choices.consequence: You handed over your details without a second thought.

choices.label: Wait — why do you need all of that?

engage_followup.message: It's simply to verify that you're the account holder. Time is limited to complete this transfer.

choices.label: I'll need to verify this independently before sharing anything.
choices.consequence: You held the line and asked to verify independently.

choices.label: Fine, here it is.
choices.consequence: The pressure worked. You gave up your details anyway.

question.message: Your details were identified through our standard verification process. I understand your caution, but time is limited to complete this transfer.

choices.label: I'd like proof of this estate and your firm before continuing.
Okay, what do I need to do?
choices.consequence: You let the vague explanation satisfy you and kept going.

question_followup.message: You may contact the estate's legal department directly to confirm — here is a direct line.

choices.label: I'll verify this independently, not through a number you've given me.
choices.consequence: You recognised that a number from the scammer isn't independent verification at all.

choices.label: Alright, I'll call this number.
choices.consequence: You called the number — straight back to the same people.

verify.message: I understand your concern, but please be aware that delaying the process could result in the funds being reassigned.

choices.label: I'm not moving forward until I verify independently. Goodbye.
choices.consequence: You didn't let the urgency change your plan.

choices.label: Okay, but make it quick then.

verify_followup.message: Wonderful. There is a small legal processing fee of £650 required before the transfer can be released.

data.payee: Okoro & Williams Legal Partners — Estate Processing
data.note: Legal processing fee. Required before final transfer release.

choices.label: A fee to receive money makes no sense. I'm out.
choices.consequence: The fee request gave it away, and you walked.

choices.label: Fine, how do I pay the fee?
choices.consequence: You agreed to pay the fee.

refuse.message: I understand your skepticism, but I assure you this is a legitimate matter. It would be a shame to miss this opportunity.

choices.label: I'm blocking and reporting this number.
choices.consequence: You didn't just disengage — you shut the door and reported it.

choices.label: Prove it, then. Send me verifiable documentation.

refuse_followup.message: Adewale sends what looks like an official letterhead document, insisting the opportunity closes today.

data.body: This letter confirms that the beneficiary transfer of £4,200,000 GBP to the verified recipient is authorised pending final processing. Failure to complete verification within 24 hours will result in reassignment of funds to alternate beneficiaries as per estate protocol 14(b).

choices.label: This doesn't check out. Blocking you now.
choices.consequence: A convincing document didn't change your mind.

choices.label: Alright, I suppose that looks legitimate enough.
choices.consequence: The fake documentation was enough to bring you back in.
